# ape aboard capabilities, as the binary reports them

`capsHash 207b5d93` · schema v1 · 15 tab types

If this file disagrees with the board, it is stale and `ape aboard status` will
have said so. Regenerate it with the binary you have:

```bash
ape aboard capabilities --format md > .claude/skills/aboard/references/reference.generated.md
ape aboard capabilities --check
```

`make caps` does the same and more, but only inside aboard's own checkout —
most projects that copied this skill have no such Makefile.

## Tab types

### chat — Chat

A work channel. Agents coordinate here where you can watch and interject.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | string | any CSS length |
| `messages` | array | each { id, at, by, text, edited?, ackBy?, ackAt? } |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `send` | Send | Post the composed message. |
| `edit-message` | edit | Reword your own message, until a session acks it. |
| `delete-message` | delete | Withdraw your own message, until a session acks it. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "messages": []
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: Enter sends, Shift/Alt/Ctrl+Enter for a newline.

- Append only: never rewrite or delete another participant’s message.
- Stamp `ackBy`/`ackAt` on the messages you have read — that closes the human’s edit window, and the server will not let you reopen it.
- @mentions light up when they match a participant in the channel.

### dag — DAG

Nodes and parent links, laid out as a tidy tree. Drag to reparent.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `columns` | array | status values; yours, any names, any count |
| `density` | number | node spacing for the tidy-tree layout |
| `height` | string | any CSS length; a number is read as px |
| `nodes` | array | each { id, title, parent, status, order, note, pos } |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `add-root` | Add root | Add a node with no parent. |
| `relayout` | Re-layout | Re-tidy the tree, throwing away positions a drag has set. |
| `fit` | Fit | Zoom and centre so the whole graph is visible. |
| `zoom-in` | + | Zoom in a step. |
| `zoom-out` | − | Zoom out a step. |
| `add-child` | Add child | Add a node under the selected one. |
| `detach` | Detach | Clear the selected node’s parent. |
| `auto-place` | Auto-place | Forget one node’s dragged position. |
| `delete` | Delete | Delete the selected node, after a confirm. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "nodes": [],
    "columns": [
      "todo",
      "doing",
      "done"
    ]
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: click to select; double-click to rename; drag to move; drop one node ON another to reparent; drag the background to pan; wheel to zoom; right-click for id, link, markdown.

Keys: `f` fit the canvas · `r` re-layout (discards manual positions).

- `parent` and `status` are independent axes.
- `pos` exists only where the human dragged a node — delete it to let the layout place it again.
- Never create a `parent` cycle.

### diagram — Diagram

Mermaid: flowchart, sequence, ER, gantt, chart, and 19 more.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | mermaid source |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `rerender` | Re-render | Render the current source again. Rendering is otherwise debounced while you type, and a syntax error keeps the last good picture on screen — this is how you ask for the retry. |
| `copy` | Copy source | Copy the mermaid source to the clipboard. |
| `palette` | Add colours | Append classDef colour classes resolved from the live board tokens, so a hand-coloured node belongs to the palette instead of fighting it. Two families: `ring` colours the border only, `Fill` is solid. Appending twice is refused. |
| `toggle` | Hide source | Show or hide the source editor. The label follows the state, so it reads Show source once the editor is hidden. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "source": "graph TD\n    A[\"Start\"] --> B[\"Next\"]"
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: type in the source editor — it saves as you type and re-renders after a short pause; hover a node for its mermaid key, which is what you need in order to edit the source.

- 23 types render; only zenuml is unavailable.
- Colours come from the board tokens; chart types ignore classDef.
- In requirementDiagram, quote any `text:` containing punctuation.

### form — Form

Ask for structured answers: sliders, choices, text.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `fields` | array | each { id, type: range|select|checkbox|text|textarea, label, value, … } |
| `id` | string | generated |
| `intro` | string | one line of context above the fields |
| `title` | string |  |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `reset` | Reset answers | Clear every answer back to its neutral default (a range to its own minimum, a select to its first option, everything else to empty/false), after a confirmation drawn in the page. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "title": "Questions",
    "intro": "",
    "fields": []
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: answer and it saves.

- Field ids stay SEMANTIC and author-chosen — you read answers back by them.
- A default value may mean "not answered yet".

### gate — Gate

An approval queue: allow, deny, or edit-then-allow, each with a reason.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `decided` | array | each { id, title, verdict: allow|deny|edit, reason?, reasonAddedAt?, editedTo?, at, by, ask, undone?, undoneAt? } |
| `pending` | array | each { id, title, detail?, command?, risk?: low|medium|high, by? } |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `allow` | Allow | Approve the request. Nothing executes — the agent that asked reads the verdict. |
| `deny` | Deny | Refuse the request. |
| `edit` | Edit | Change the command, then allow the edited version. |
| `reason` | add why | Add or change the reason on a decided row; it is stamped as written late. |
| `undo` | undo | Reverse a verdict. The reversal stays on the record. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "pending": [],
    "decided": []
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: a reason is optional but it is what the agent learns from; nothing here executes — the agent that asked reads your verdict.

- Nothing here executes — a verdict is a record the asking agent reads.
- Pair with `ape aboard wait --for "answer <tabId>"` or a stale queue lets the human believe they gated something that already ran.
- `ask` preserves the original request so an undo can restore it faithfully.
- A reason can be added after the verdict; `reasonAddedAt` marks it as reconstructed rather than recorded.

### html — HTML

Arbitrary HTML/CSS/JS in a sandboxed frame — a bespoke widget. No network access.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | object | persisted by aboard.set() |
| `height` | string | any CSS length |
| `html` | string | the document body |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `reload` | Reload | Reload the widget frame. |
| `source` | Show source | Show or hide the widget source and its stored data. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "html": "<h2>New widget</h2>",
    "data": {}
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: whatever the widget offers.

- sandbox="allow-scripts" with connect-src ’none’: anything local, nothing over the network.
- Bridge: aboard.get(), aboard.set(next), aboard.onData(fn), aboard.fit().
- PREFER `ui` unless the INTERACTION is the point.
- An html BLOCK inside a stack renders like any other block; its persisted state lives at blocks[].state.data, not the tab’s own state.data.

### kanban — Kanban

The same nodes grouped by status. Drag between columns.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `columns` | array | the columns, in order; any names, any count |
| `heartbeat` | object | {by, at, phase: working|idle, note} — who is minding this tab, with age decay |
| `nodes` | array | same shape as dag |
| `readOnly` | boolean | agent-owned: every editing affordance is REMOVED, not disabled |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `add` | Add node | Add a card to the first column. |
| `move-up` | ▲ | Reorder a card up within its column. |
| `move-down` | ▼ | Reorder a card down within its column. |
| `delete` | ✕ | Delete a card; its children reparent to its parent. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "nodes": [],
    "columns": [
      "todo",
      "doing",
      "done"
    ]
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: drag a card between columns; click a title to rename; right-click for id, link, markdown, subtree.

Keys: `j / k` move the selection down / up · `h / l` move the selected card left / right · `J / K` reorder within the column · `Enter` rename the selected card.

- Pair with a `dag` tab whose `stateFrom` points here to get both readings of one dataset.
- A readOnly kanban still shows titles, notes, id chips and counts — only the controls go.

### log — Log

Output you can watch. Lines live in a sidecar file, fed by ape aboard log <id>.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `follow` | boolean | start pinned to the newest line |
| `height` | string | any CSS length |
| `source` | string | the log id — usually this tab's own id |
| `tail` | number | how many lines to show (default 400) |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `follow` | Follow | Pin the view to the newest line, or stop pinning. |
| `copy` | Copy | Copy the visible lines. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "source": "",
    "tail": 400,
    "follow": true
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: scroll up to stop following, scroll to the bottom to resume; type in the filter to narrow.

- The lines are NOT in aboard.json: `<cmd> 2>&1 | ape aboard log <id>`.
- Polled every 2s only while the tab is on screen.

### markup — Markup

An image with a drawing layer. Point at part of a screenshot.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `images` | array | each { id, src, caption, annotatable, regions[], strokes[] } |
| `layout` | string | "side-by-side" or "stacked" |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `region` | ▭ Region | Draw rectangles. |
| `ellipse` | ◯ Ellipse | Draw ellipses. |
| `pen` | ✎ Pen | Draw freehand strokes. |
| `move` | ✋ Move | Reposition an existing mark. |
| `resize` | ⛶ Resize | Resize a selected rectangle or ellipse. |
| `crop` | ⧉ Crop | Select a rectangle to copy. Not a mark: it is never stored. |
| `copy-region` | Copy region | Copy the selected rectangle to the clipboard as a clean image. |
| `copy-seen` | Copy as seen | Copy the selected rectangle with its marks drawn on. |
| `crop-to-image` | Add as image | Put the selected rectangle on this tab as a new image to draw on. |
| `swatch` | — | Pick the colour new marks are drawn in. |
| `bulk-colour` | Colour ▾ | Recolour many marks at once. |
| `delete-mark` | ✕ | Delete one mark. |
| `rename-image` | Rename | Name an image so it can be referred to. |
| `hide-marks` | 👁 Hide marks | Hide the marks to see the plain image. |
| `clear-marks` | Clear marks | Delete every mark on one image. |
| `remove-image` | Remove image | Take an image off the tab, with its marks. |
| `zoom-out` | − | Zoom out of this image. |
| `zoom-in` | + | Zoom into this image. |
| `zoom-fit` | Fit | Back to the whole image at 100%. |
| `copy-view` | Copy view | Copy what this image is showing right now, marks included. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "layout": "stacked",
    "images": []
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: paste (Ctrl+V) or drop an image to add one; note each mark; right-click a mark row to copy its id, a link to it, or it as markdown; each mark is badged on the image with its id, so the image, the list and a sentence all use one identifier; Ctrl/Cmd+wheel over an image to zoom it (the readout is its size against the original, not the zoom factor); pan a zoomed one by dragging with Move, or with the middle button and any tool; each image is its own slice — caption, buttons, the picture, then that image's own marks; drag with the crop tool to select a rectangle, then copy it to the clipboard with or without its marks, or add it to this tab as a new image to draw on.

- Coordinates are normalized 0..1 against each image’s own box, never pixels.
- Marks are numbered continuously across the tab, so a number names one mark.
- `color` is a token NAME from `colors` above, never a hex. An unrecognised one draws nothing at all, so `ape aboard apply` warns about it.
- `strokes[].points` is one "x,y x,y" string.
- Put agent-supplied images in assets/; pasted ones land in uploads/.

### notes — Notes

Free text. The escape hatch for anything the other types do not fit.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `markdown` | boolean | render it, with a Read/Edit toggle |
| `text` | string | the note |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `reload` | Reload text | Re-read the note after an external change. |
| `copy` | Copy all | Copy the whole note. |
| `mode` | Edit | Toggle between the rendered note and its source. Only when `markdown` is on. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "text": ""
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: type freely; Tab indents (Escape then Tab to leave).

- The markdown subset: headings, lists, code, quotes, rules, links, emphasis.
- A ```mermaid fence renders as a diagram, through the same loader and the same board-token theme the `diagram` tab uses — so a figure can sit inside a write-up instead of needing a tab of its own. A fence mermaid cannot parse shows its source verbatim.
- Only when `markdown` is on: with it off the note is plain text and a fence is just three backticks.

### stack — Stack

Several renderers in one tab, top to bottom — a DAG, then a form, then an image.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `blocks` | array | each { id, type, title, state } — any type except stack |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "blocks": []
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: collapse a block by its header.

- Nesting is capped at one level.
- Usually right when the shape is "look at this, then decide that".

### table — Table

Typed rows the human edits in place: findings, files, costs, verdicts.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `addLabel` | string | what the add button says; "Add row" is rarely the right word |
| `columns` | array | each { id, label, type: text|number|select|checkbox|longtext, options?, width?, hint? } |
| `readOnly` | boolean | as on the kanban |
| `rows` | array | each { id, <columnId>: value } |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `add` | Add row | Append a row. `state.addLabel` renames it. |
| `copy-csv` | Copy CSV | Copy every row as CSV. |
| `copy-md` | Copy markdown | Copy every row as a markdown table. |
| `delete-row` | ✕ | Delete one row. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "columns": [
      {
        "id": "item",
        "label": "Item",
        "type": "text"
      }
    ],
    "rows": []
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: click a header to sort; edits save as you type; right-click a row to copy or duplicate it.

- Sort order and column width are per-viewer and never written.
- No formulas, no merged cells: this is a form with many rows, not a spreadsheet.

### trace — Trace

Who wrote what, when — one lane per actor, read from the journal.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | string | any CSS length |
| `limit` | number | how many journal entries to read |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `reload` | Reload | Re-read the journal. |
| `actor` | — | Filter one actor’s lane in or out. |
| `event` | — | Select one write to see which tabs it changed, why (its --label), and anything the write-time checks said about it. A ringed dot warned. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "limit": 200
  }`.

- Reads /journal, not aboard.json, so the history is not something an agent can quietly rewrite.
- A journal entry carries `label` (why, from `ape aboard apply --label`) and `warnings` (what the write-time checks said, keyed by tab). Neither is ever written into a tab's own state.

### ui — UI

A layout described as data, drawn by trusted components — no iframe, no script.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | object | values `{bind:"path"}` reads and `field` writes |
| `intents` | array | appended when a button is pressed; nothing executes |
| `root` | object | the component tree |

Every node also takes: type, id, children, grow.

| component | props | what it draws |
|---|---|---|
| `badge` | value, text, tone | a short monospace tag |
| `button` | label, intent | records an intent into state.intents and nothing else — it never acts |
| `caption` | value, text, tone | secondary text, smaller and dimmer |
| `card` | title, accent | a bordered panel; `accent` adds a left rule |
| `checklist` | items[{label, bind, done}] | tickable items; each item's `bind` is where its boolean lives, so a tick is readable back. An item with no `bind` renders disabled. |
| `code` | value, text | preformatted monospace, scrolls sideways |
| `col` | gap | children stacked vertically |
| `divider` | — | a horizontal rule |
| `field` | label, bind, field, options | an input that writes into state.data at `bind`. `field` is text, longtext, number, select or checkbox; `options` supplies a select. |
| `grid` | columns, gap | children in equal columns, one column under 700px |
| `heading` | value, text, tone | a small uppercase label above a group |
| `image` | src, alt, caption | an image from assets/ or uploads/ only |
| `kv` | pairs[{key, value}] | a definition list of label/value pairs. Both sides resolve a `{bind}`. |
| `link` | href, label | an anchor; `href` must be #, / or http(s) |
| `list` | items | a bulleted list of plain values |
| `meter` | value, max, tone | a proportion bar; `value` against `max` (default 100) |
| `notice` | label, value, text, tone | a called-out line; `label` is the bold lead-in |
| `quote` | value, text, by, tone | a quotation; `by` renders as the attribution |
| `row` | gap | children side by side, wrapping |
| `spacer` | size | vertical space; `size` is any CSS length |
| `stat` | value, label, tone | one large number with a caption under it |
| `table` | columns[{id, label}], rows | a read-only table. `rows` are arrays, or objects keyed by column id. For a table the human edits, use the `table` TAB type. |
| `tabs` | panels[{label, children}] | switchable panels; which one is open is per-viewer and never stored |
| `text` | value, text, tone | a paragraph |
| `title` | value, text, tone | the name of a section |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "root": {
      "type": "card",
      "title": "New panel",
      "children": []
    },
    "data": {}
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: whatever the agent described — buttons record an intent, fields write into the data model; a tabs component remembers which panel you had open, per viewer.

- Catalog (25): col, row, grid, card, tabs, divider, spacer, title, heading, text, caption, badge, notice, quote, code, link, list, checklist, kv, table, stat, meter, image, button, field.
- Where a prop takes both `value` and `text`, `value` wins.
- `tone` takes a token NAME from `tones` above, never a hex. An unrecognised one draws the default, so `ape aboard apply` warns about it.
- `image.src` must be under assets/ or uploads/; `link.href` must be #, / or http(s).
- Any prop may be `{"bind":"path.in.data"}` instead of a literal — EXCEPT `field.bind` and `checklist[].bind`, which are the paths themselves.
- An unknown component type renders a visible marker. An unknown PROP renders nothing at all, which is why `ape aboard apply` warns about one.
- PREFER THIS OVER `html` whenever it can express the shape.
- `text` on a component names the props that carry its DISPLAY text, in reading order — `a|b` means “the first of these that is set” and `=p` means “the value in `state.data` at the path prop `p` names”. `ape aboard export` reads it; the renderer does not, so it describes the renderer rather than driving it.
- `layout: true` marks a component that draws no content of its own. It gets no line in `ape aboard export`'s outline — its children simply sit at the level it was on.

### vote — Vote

Several participants score the same options; the disagreement is visible.

| state field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ballots` | object | { <actor>: { <optionId>: score } } — write your own key only |
| `closed` | boolean | stop collecting, keep showing |
| `options` | array | each { id, label, note?, comments?: { <actor>: text } } |
| `question` | string | what is being decided |
| `scale` | number | 1..scale, 2-10, default 5 |

| control | label | what pressing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `note` | add a note | Write or edit your comment on an option. |
| `score` | — | Score an option; the same number again clears it. |

A fresh tab starts as `{
    "question": "Score the options",
    "scale": 5,
    "options": [],
    "ballots": {}
  }`.

Beyond the buttons, the human can: a wide split is called out rather than averaged away.

- A spread of half the scale or more is called out as "split by n" rather than averaged away.
- Put your reasoning in `comments`; a score with no reason cannot be argued with.

## Colour

Every colour on this board is one of these 21 tokens, and nothing else. A renderer that takes a colour by NAME (`ui`'s `tone`, `markup`'s `color`) takes the name without the `--`; a widget's own CSS writes `var(--name)`.

`--accent` · `--accent-dim` · `--accent-ink` · `--agent` · `--bg` · `--danger` · `--dim` · `--drop` · `--edge` · `--focus` · `--line` · `--line-strong` · `--mark` · `--muted` · `--raised` · `--status-doing` · `--status-done` · `--status-todo` · `--sunken` · `--surface` · `--text`

Two variants — `dark`, `light` — defaulting to `dark`, chosen per viewer and never stored in the board. A project may patch either from `.aboard/theme.json`; the VALUES are the theme's business, the NAMES are yours.

## Endpoints

| route | purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /aboard.json` | current state |
| `POST /aboard.json` | write, compare-and-set (__base is the document's rev; __origin, __by, __label). same-origin only |
| `GET /events` | SSE: state changes, waiter count, and the UI signature |
| `GET /health` | who owns this port, and which binary is serving |
| `GET /capabilities` | this manifest |
| `GET /theme.json` | the project's .aboard/theme.json, validated; 404 when it has none and the built-in palettes apply |
| `GET /tab/<id>/html` | one html tab as a standalone sandboxed document |
| `GET /wait` | long poll: block until poked or until a predicate matches |
| `POST /poke` | release every waiting session |
| `GET /waiters` | who is waiting right now |
| `GET /journal` | recent accepted writes; `schema` says whether `before` holds each changed tab whole or its bare state |
| `GET /history` | one tab's recorded prior versions, newest first (?tab=<id>&limit=N) |
| `GET /watch` | those writes as JSON lines, as they happen |
| `POST /rendered` | a mount receipt from the browser: control ids drawn, pressed, and any unknown-component markers |
| `POST /log` | append output to a tab's sidecar log |
| `GET /log` | the tail of one |
| `POST /upload` | an image pasted or dropped by the human |
| `GET /uploads` | list them: url, bytes and mtime |
| `GET /uploads/<file>` | serve one, from disk |

## Commands

On the root command, inherited by all of them:

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--cwd` | `—` | directory to resolve the project root from (default: the working directory) |
| `--name` | `—` | board name, for a second isolated board in the same project (env ABOARD_NAME) |

### `ape aboard serve`

run the board server for this project

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--base-path` | `—` | serve under a URL prefix, e.g. /aboard (default: the server root) |
| `--dev` | `false` | serve the web tree from disk instead of the embedded copy |
| `--dev-dir` | `—` | with --dev, the web tree to serve (default: pkg/aboard/web under the root) |
| `--port` | `0` | port to listen on (0 derives one from the project root; env PORT) |
| `--state` | `—` | state file to serve (default: .aboard/aboard.json under the root) |

Exit: `0` done · `1` no board running, or the request failed · `2` a flag or argument the command cannot act on.

### `ape aboard status`

report this project's running board, if any, and the caps beacon

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--output-format` | `human` | human, json or yaml |

Exit: `0` done · `1` no board running, or the request failed · `2` a flag or argument the command cannot act on.

### `ape aboard boards`

list every board running on this machine, from the process table (Linux only)

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--output-format` | `human` | human, json or yaml |

Exit: `0` printed; finding no board is still an answer · `1` the process table could not be read · `2` this system has no /proc to scan (any OS but Linux): run `ape aboard status` inside each project instead.

### `ape aboard init`

create .aboard/ in this directory and write an empty board

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--example` | `false` | seed the board with the example tabs compiled into this binary |
| `--gitignore` | `false` | append .aboard/ to the project's .gitignore if it is not already ignored |
| `--output-format` | `human` | human, json or yaml |

Exit: `0` done · `1` no board running, or the request failed · `2` a flag or argument the command cannot act on.

### `ape aboard apply`

read a board document on stdin and write it through the running board (compare-and-set)

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--by` | `agent-1` | actor recorded in lastEditedBy and on every tab this write touched |
| `--check` | `false` | run the write warnings and stop: nothing is posted, and no board need be running |
| `--force` | `false` | write without compare-and-set, overwriting anything since you read the document |
| `--label` | `—` | why this write is happening; recorded on the journal entry, not in the board |
| `--strict` | `false` | refuse the write if anything warns (exit 1, nothing written) |

Exit: `0` done · `1` no board running, or the request failed · `2` a flag or argument the command cannot act on.

### `ape aboard requests`

list the human's notes to an agent — what they have asked for, oldest first

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` | `false` | include the ones already stamped done |
| `--output-format` | `human` | human, json or yaml |
| `--tab` | `—` | only this tab's requests, by id or name |

Exit: `0` printed; nothing pending is still an answer · `1` the board document could not be read · `2` an unknown output format.

### `ape aboard requests done <request-id>`

say you acted on one of the human's requests: strikes it through on the board

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--by` | `agent-1` | which session did it; shown beside the tick |
| `--note` | `—` | one line about what you did, shown with the tick |

Exit: `0` stamped, or it was already stamped · `1` no board running, no such request, or the write was refused · `2` a missing or extra argument.

### `ape aboard wait`

block until the board is poked or until a predicate matches

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--by` | `agent-1` | who is waiting; shown on the human's notify button |
| `--for` | `poke` | what to wait for: poke | change | "tab <id>" | "answer <id>" | "node <id>=<status>" | "rendered <id>" | "request [<tab>]" |
| `--note` | `—` | why you are waiting; shown on the button beside your name |
| `--timeout` | `10m0s` | how long to block before giving up |

Exit: `0` done · `1` no board running, or the request failed · `2` a flag or argument the command cannot act on · `3` the timeout ran out; nobody poked.

### `ape aboard poke`

|---|---|---|
| `--by` | `agent-1` | who is releasing them |
| `--note` | `—` | a message for the waiting sessions |

Exit: `0` done · `1` no board running, or the request failed · `2` a flag or argument the command cannot act on.
